0.0.n: A formal, weighty way to refer to oneself and one's group.

0.1.n: Links 我々 to 目的, showing whose objective it is.

0.2.n: Names the goal the speaker's group aims to achieve.

0.3.n: Marks the group's objective as the topic being explained.

0.5.n: Refers to a particular state in this fictional setting, listed as an intended alliance member.

0.7.n: Refers to another state in this fictional setting, listed as an intended alliance member.

0.9.n: 法国 is the designation of a religious state in this fictional setting.

0.11.n: Placed before a name to identify the opponent.

0.12.n: A proper name identifying the opponent the proposed alliance would face.

0.13.n: Links the preceding opposition phrase to ため, introducing the alliance's purpose.

0.14.n: In のための, explains what the proposed alliance is intended to accomplish.

0.15.n: Connects the purpose expressed with ため to the following noun 大連合.

0.16.n: 大 adds the sense of large scale to 連合, emphasizing the proposed coalition's scope.

0.17.n: Links 大連合 to 設立, identifying what will be established.

0.18.n: A noun naming the act of creating the alliance.

0.19.n: Plain declarative ending that firmly identifies the objective.

1.0.n: Refers to the conflict or struggle under discussion.

1.1.n: Marks これ as the topic of the statement.

1.2.n: 国家 means nation; 間 adds the sense of relations between them.

1.3.n: Connects 国家間 to 争い, describing the dispute as one involving nations.

1.4.n: A noun for conflict, here describing the interpretation the speaker rejects.

1.5.n: Combines with はない to form the plain negative of だ after a noun.

1.6.n: Works with で and ない in ではない, rejecting the description 国家間の争い.

1.7.n: Completes ではない, making the statement negative.

2.0.n: Refers to humanity collectively, rather than an individual person.

2.1.n: Introduces 人 as the name or identity of the species.

2.2.n: Refers to humans as a distinct group of beings in this setting.

2.3.n: Links the human species to its continued existence.

2.4.n: A formal noun emphasizing continued existence rather than disappearance.

2.5.n: Marks 存続 as what is put on the line with かけた.

2.6.n: Past form of かける describing 戦い; here it indicates the stakes, not necessarily a finished battle.

2.8.n: Names what this battle aims to protect.

2.9.n: Marks 未来 as the thing affected by 守る; English has no direct equivalent.

2.10.n: Plain form placed before 戦い to describe the battle's purpose.

2.11.n: The noun described by both the survival-at-stake phrase and 未来を守る.

2.12.n: Plain declarative ending; the subject remains understood from the preceding line.

0.lit: Our objective: Empire, Kingdom, Theocracy—the establishment of a grand alliance for opposing Ainz Ooal Gown.
0.tip: The main structure is 目的は…設立だ: the objective is establishment, with everything between specifying the alliance.

1.lit: This is not a dispute between nations.
1.tip: After a noun, ではない is the plain negative of だ: is not.

2.lit: It is a future-protecting battle putting the survival of the species called humans on the line.
2.tip: Both descriptions come before 戦い: what is at stake and what the battle protects.
